chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 248 – Sun Xiaoqin: A Mother’s Love Becomes a Farewell
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang gives his hallucinated mother gold, earrings, and a final goodbye. The warmth of the hospital room crushes him harder than any demon ever could.
og_title: He Brought Gold from Another World, But It Was a Goodbye Gift
og_description: In chapter 248 of Dao Gui Yi Xian, the true horror isn’t a monster—it’s a mother’s love. Li Huowang must choose between a hallucinated home and a blood-soaked reality.
twitter_title: He left his mother with gold, earrings, and a lie. Then he ate the Black Tai Sui and wept.
twitter_description: Chapter 248: Li Huowang says goodbye to his mother, gives away all his treasure, and forces himself to return to the Dao-Twisted World. The saddest chapter in a long time.

lore_anchors.definition: A grotesque, parasitic flesh-substance produced by corrupted cultivation; in the Dao-Twisted World, consuming it can suppress madness, but it is a living, bleeding thing that exacts a cost.
Li Huowang’s mother in the modern-world hallucination; fiercely protective, stubbornly optimistic, and the emotional anchor he chooses to leave behind.
A pair of green jade earrings Li Huowang intended as a birthday gift for Yang Na; he hands them to his mother to pass along as a final gesture of apology.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang leave the hospital hallucination if it feels so real?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He recognizes it as a hallucination tied to the Black Tai Sui and remembers that Bai Lingmiao’s bruised face was real. He chooses responsibility over comfort, even though it destroys him to do so.

Within the novel’s framework, she is part of a hallucinatory episode driven by the Black Tai Sui. But the chapter intentionally blurs the line—her love and grief are expressed in ways that feel genuine, which is the source of the tragedy.
